II. Potential options for elements towards an international legally binding instrument, based on a comprehensive approach that addresses the full life cycle of plastics as called for by United Nations Environment Assembly resolution 5/14
B. Core obligations, control measures and voluntary approaches (including annexes, if any)
1. Possible core obligation: phasing out and/or reducing the supply of, demand for and use of primary plastic polymers
2. Possible core obligation: banning, phasing out and/or reducing the use of problematic and avoidable plastic products
3. Possible core obligation: banning, phasing out and/or reducing the production, consumption and use of chemicals and polymers of concern
5. Possible core obligation: strengthening waste management
6. Possible core obligation: fostering design for circularity
7. Possible core obligation: encouraging reduce, reuse and repair of plastic products and packaging
8. Possible core obligation: promoting the use of safe, sustainable alternatives and substitutes
9. Possible core obligation: eliminating the release and emission of plastics to water, soil and air
10. Possible core obligation: addressing existing plastic pollution
11. Possible core obligation: facilitating a just transition, including an inclusive transition of the informal waste sector
12. Possible core obligation: protecting human health from the adverse effects of plastic pollution
4. Technology transfer on mutually agreed terms
